## The M43 Schism: Skill vs. Gear

The debate over the relevance of Micro Four Thirds (M43) cameras continues to simmer on 4chan, revealing a stark divide between purists and pragmatists. One camp argues that GoPro is the only entity truly leveraging the system’s small form factor, while criticizing M43 enthusiasts for overspending on high-end lenses and software. Critics mock the system for being "too sharp" and prone to moiré patterns due to a lack of anti-aliasing filters, suggesting buyers opt for affordable kit zooms or the Fujifilm X-M5 instead.

Adding a layer of corporate satire to the technical argument, a Canon executive jokingly claimed that "auto mode" was rebranded as "girlfriend mode" to appease BlackRock’s DEI squad. Ultimately, the consensus leans toward dismissing these complaints as "skill issues," asserting that most users are not professionals requiring pro-level equipment. This sentiment aligns with a broader community motto emerging on the /p/ board: "gear only matters if your photo doesn't suck." Despite this philosophical shift toward skill over specs, moderation remains minimal, with moderators primarily stepping in to ban complaints about specific recurring users rather than enforcing strict technical standards.

## Nikon Z5IIC Rumors and Zoom Addiction

On the hardware front, speculation is mounting regarding Nikon’s upcoming compact full-frame camera, the Z5IIC. Positioned as a direct competitor to the Sony a7c series, rumors suggest a 24 MP sensor with in-body image stabilization (IBIS) housed in a rangefinder-style body without a viewfinder hump. Sentiment is mixed; some users are excited for a non-Sony compact option, while others fear it is merely a "parts bin camera" relying on aging Expeed 7 architecture. Physical comparisons note the V2 version is fatter than the original Z5, lacking certain sensor variants.

Meanwhile, users upgrading to the Nikon P1100 superzoom are testing its limits. High-quality macro shots of *Amanita muscaria* mushrooms and textured frogs on decaying leaves serve as proof of concept for the lens’s optical performance. The discussion highlights a "zoom addiction," with users eager to see if the camera can satisfy their need for extreme reach without sacrificing detail in natural woodland lighting.

## Philosophy, Retro Vibes, and Tech Updates

A fascinating philosophical thread on Bsky explores **physicalism** and the concept of the soul. Users note that many non-theists experience a "teenage existential freakout" upon realizing they are physicalists, yet often cling to a soul-like concept, causing confusion in debates. This overlaps with discussions on AI regulation, criticized by some as "mandatory censorship" driven by government-cartel creations.

In the tech world, @word-sys released **PULS v0.9.4**, a major update for the Linux terminal monitoring tool. After a decade of development, the update introduces granular settings persistence, multi-language support, and a hierarchical process tree view. Significant performance gains include replacing file I/O with direct syscalls, reducing idle CPU usage to ~0.1%. The tool now supports GPU telemetry for NVIDIA, AMD, and Intel cards and features new color themes.

## Quick Hits

*   **Celebrations:** @Oksii celebrated her 11th wedding anniversary and raised €333 for friend Tony Smerdoochi. @Will Smith and @austin_walker also sent birthday greetings to @Carolyn Petit, marking her 50th birthday.
*   **Forest Atmosphere:** Photographers @Odd-Habit196 and @IamaFungii shared serene images of forests after rain, highlighting the calming aesthetics of damp woodlands.
*   **Vintage Poetry:** User @LOWapproachg posted "Awaiting fall," a poem by "Primoplan" paired with imagery from a Primoplan 58 1.9 lens, celebrating the sensory shift from summer to autumn.
*   **Holiday Gallery:** The "/rpt/ Unsuccessful Tries Edition" on 4chan continues to serve as a gallery for holiday photos, with users posting generic seasonal images rather than failed attempts.
*   **Urban Aesthetics:** A commenter praised a specific photo for capturing gritty, visually complex urban environments, expressing a dislike for sterile, "clean and dull" modern cities.
*   **Media Recommendations:** Users on /p/ exchanged media recommendations, highlighting Amazon Prime titles like *Helluva Boss* and *Hazbin Hotel*, with notes on the accuracy of Amazon’s analytics.

representative_texts: @word-sys - Linux, GNU/Linux, free software... — PULS v0.9.4 Optimization & Feature Update Released — Big update for PULS , after a decade now it has reached v0.9.4 update . This update is a major feature, performance, and hardware telemetry release. I started sharing development stages and tests on my YouTube channel where you can check out more details for current and future releases.   This update introduces a Granular Settings Modal & Configuration Persistence (F2 / Shift+S) which lets you configure your environment directly inside the TUI. You can customize Interface Language, Color Theme, Default Startup Tab, Temperature Units (Celsius / Fahrenheit), Telemetry Refresh Rate (500ms - 5000ms), and Process Tree defaults, all automatically persisted to ~/.config/puls/config.ini .   Another major addition is Multi-Language Expansion (7 Languages) . PULS now includes full, native localization for English (default), Turkish, French, German, Spanish, Italian, and Russian with automatic LANG / LC_ALL environment detection on startup and instant runtime cycling ( L / l ).   I also added Full Terminal Mouse Event Capture . You can now click any header tab directly to navigate, click the Settings badge, and smoothly scroll process tables, active socket lists, journal logs, and modal windows using the mouse wheel — protected by a panic hook that guarantees safe terminal state restoration upon exit.   Added a Hierarchical Process Tree View & POSIX Signal Selector . Easily toggle between a flat sortable list and parent-child tree view ( t ) with standard branch glyphs ( ├─ , └─ ). You can send POSIX signals ( SIGTERM , SIGKILL , SIGHUP , SIGSTOP , SIGCONT , SIGINT ) via an interactive modal ( k / F9 ), and dynamically adjust scheduling niceness on the fly ( [ to raise priority, ] to lower priority).   Added an Extended Process Inspector (Enter) that opens a deep-dive multi-view modal displaying all open file descriptors ( /proc/[pid]/fd ), active socket counts, and per-thread CPU utilization and execution states ( /proc/[pid]/task ).   Added Filesystem Inodes & Active Network Socket Mapping , reporting partition inode capacity and mount flags via zero-dependency statvfs , per-process disk read/write throughput rates ( /proc/[pid]/io ), and active TCP/UDP socket endpoint tracking parsed natively from /proc/net/ .   This update also includes deep optimizations and important improvements:     Massive CPU & Memory Optimizations: Replaced /proc/[pid]/stat file reading with a direct native getpriority syscall to eliminate 500+ file I/O operations per second, cached translation dictionaries, and shifted string formatting on-demand strictly to visible viewport rows.   Stutter-Free Decoupled UI Loop: Separated the 30 FPS rendering pipeline from background telemetry queries and eliminated busy-wait loops, reducing idle CPU usage to ~0.1%.   GPU Telemetry & Throttling Flags: Added power limit vs current draw, PCIe link generation/width, fan RPM, and thermal throttling flags for NVIDIA, AMD, and Intel GPUs.   Hardware Power & NUMA Topology: Battery health, charging wattage, AC status, CPU frequency scaling governors, and NUMA node core affinity support for systems with up to 128+ cores.   3 New Curated Color Themes: Added Dracula, Solarized Dark, and High Contrast alongside Default, Dark Blue, and Light.   Multi-Architecture Release Pipeline: Automated CI/CD builds for static standalone MUSL binaries and Debian packages ( .deb ) for both AMD64 ( x86_64 ) and ARM64 ( aarch64 ).   Zero New Dependencies: All new features were implemented using the Rust standard library and native Linux kernel interfaces without bloating binary size with external crates.     You can download the .deb package, static portable MUSL binary, or build from source directly on the GitHub Releases page .   Thanks to everyone who supports this project with their ideas, feedback, and bug reports. I hope this helps all Linux users monitor and manage their systems with ease, thank you :)   Posted by u/word-sys · [comments]
clusters.summary: User @word-sys announces the release of PULS v0.9.4, a major update for the Linux terminal-based system monitoring tool after a decade of development. Key features include granular settings persistence, multi-language support for seven languages, and full terminal mouse event capture for navigation and scrolling. The update introduces a hierarchical process tree view, POSIX signal selectors, and an extended process inspector displaying file descriptors and socket counts. Significant performance optimizations were implemented, such as replacing file I/O with direct syscalls and decoupling the UI loop to reduce idle CPU usage to ~0.1%. Additional additions include GPU telemetry for NVIDIA, AMD, and Intel cards, hardware power monitoring, and new color themes like Dracula and Solarized Dark. The tool is available as static MUSL binaries or Debian packages for both AMD64 and ARM64 architectures, featuring zero new dependencies.
